messages:
IncidentBot: PAGER ALERT — routing-service p99 latency breach detected across eu-west-1 and us-east-1. Symptoms: streaming stalls, connection spikes, tail requests > 5s. Pager fired at 1768612345.
Mira: I’m paged, looking. pulling up router dashboards and recent deploys.
Raj: +1 on page. Saw a sharp rise in per-route tail at ~17:22 UTC, p95 mildly up but p99 huge. affecting streaming and non-streaming paths.
Isabel: Routing policy rollout 2026-03-14 at 16:58 UTC touched weighted-steering v3 -> v4, targeting hot-key smoothing. Could be related.
Mira: Copy — running quick query against router metrics: `sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{le=\"5\"}[5m])) by (route)` and looking for skew.
SRE-Tools: quick snapshot: top 3 affected routes: /v1/generate-stream, /v1/chat/stream, /v1/embed (bulk). eu-west-1 node group rg-router-7 shows abnormally high queue_depth and retransmits.
Raj: Any evidence of hot partitioning? previous incidents had similar signature when policy created tight stickiness.
Isabel: v4 policy added affinity_key hashing by customer_id mod 64 and a fallback rule. If routing keys are skewed, can create hot partitions on a few workers. logs show a lot of hits to shard-12 in eu-west-1.
Mira: Can we temporarily disable v4 and roll back to v3? That would remove policy skew risk and confirm.
Isabel: I can revert to v3 with a single command — initiating canary rollback to 0% v4 now.
OpsBot: deploy: routing-policy-v4 -> decreasing traffic 100% -> 0% (initiated by Isabel).
Mira: Monitoring now — queue_depth on rg-router-7 dropping from 420 -> 80 over last 30s. p99 for /v1/generate-stream dropping from 5.2s -> 1.1s.
Raj: Good. Does customer impact look like errors or just latency?
SRE-Tools: error rate only marginally increased (+0.2%), majority is latency/stalls, streaming frames delayed. Customers on high-concurrency streams are most affected.
Lucas: Product note — two enterprise customers reported intermittent stalls; ticket ids 8921 and 8930. We should update them with mitigation steps and ETA.
Mira: For now, continue rollback to 0% and keep autoscaling up. I’m also forcing an extra router pool spin-up in eu-west-1 (scale +2).
Isabel: spin-up in progress. also found a config: `max_concurrent_streams_per_worker` set to 16 in v4 but 64 in v3 — that explains lower capacity under v4. v4 intended to protect single noisy customers but was too aggressive.
Raj: That aligns. So failure mode: policy changed per-worker concurrency -> hot shard due to hashing -> queue backlog -> tail latency spike.
Mira: Immediate mitigation summary: rollback policy v4 -> v3 (done), scale router pool +2 (in progress), temporarily increase `max_concurrent_streams_per_worker` to 64 in config manager for eu-west-1.
OpsBot: scale: router-pool-eu-west-1 +2 nodes (completed).
SRE-Tools: config patch applied to eu-west-1: `max_concurrent_streams_per_worker=64` (applied).
Mira: Observing metrics: p99 overall for affected routes down to ~900ms, streaming stalls dropping. continuing to monitor for 15m.
Isabel: Opening a follow-up PR to adjust v4 to use less aggressive per-worker limits and add telemetry for per-shard occupancy.
Raj: Handing off to Night SRE for 3-hour watch. I’ll prepare a short incident summary for the on-call rotation.
Mira: I’ll do handoff in 5m — taking notes: root cause likely routing policy v4 with aggressive concurrency limit + skewed hashing distribution producing hot shard. Rollback + scale + config change returned system to baseline.
Lucas: Customer comms: please send a note to affected customers summarizing impact, mitigation, and next steps (remediation timeline). I can draft a template.
Isabel: Attaching relevant logs snippet (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-14T16:59:12Z] router: route=/v1/generate-stream shard=12 worker=rg-router-7 queue_depth=389 conn_latency=4200ms
[2026-03-14T17:00:03Z] policy-eval: routing_policy=v4 affinity_key=customer_foo hash=12
[2026-03-14T17:01:45Z] router: worker=rg-router-8 queue_depth=45 conn_latency=120ms
```
Mira: Will create incident channel and link runbook entries. Also recommend we flag policy rollouts that change concurrency caps as needing extra canary steps and runbook checks.
SRE-Tools: created incident-1768612345 channel and pinned runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/router-routing-policy.md
Raj: Handoff: I’m paged off in 10m, Mira will be primary. Mira — any outstanding mitigation tasks you want me to leave?
Mira: Leave monitoring alerts on for p95/p99 and queue_depth; escalation threshold: p99 > 2s for 5m. Also confirm the v4 PR includes a staging rollout with traffic-pressure tests.
Raj: done. taking off-call.
Mira: Noted. I’m posting a short customer-impact blurb: "We observed elevated tail latency affecting streaming responses in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 between ~16:58-17:12 UTC due to a routing policy rollout. We rolled back the policy and scaled routing pools; latency has returned to baseline. Engineering is preparing a fix and will follow up with remediation timeline."
Lucas: Thanks. Please tag me on the postmortem when you have a draft.
Isabel: I’ll own the policy fix and PR. Will include telemetry additions and a stricter canary for concurrency changes.
SRE-Tools: closing temporary mitigation tasks and setting follow-up todo: postmortem, customer comms, policy change PR, additional canary tests.
Mira: Marking incident as mitigated at 1768613600 — metrics stable. Leaving channel open for postmortem notes.
IncidentBot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigated by rollback and scaling at 1768613600. severity: sev2.
Mira: Postmortem owners: Mira (ops lead), Isabel (policy fix), Raj (oncall coordination), Lucas (customer comms). Expected postmortem draft by 2026-03-16.
Raj: Thanks team. back to rotation.
Mira: End of thread — adding a couple of action items: 1) require concurrency-cap changes in routing policy PRs to have explicit canary + perf tests, 2) add per-shard heatmap to router dashboards, 3) document rollback playbook for routing policies.
Lucas: I’ll coordinate customer update drafts.
Isabel: PR opened: https://git.redwood/policies/merge_requests/987 (WIP).
SRE-Tools: archived incident artifacts to /incidents/1768612345/artifacts (metrics, logs, configs).
